per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at both termini of the entry construct. In free 5P12-RANTES-E66S at 37 °C, pH 3.8, Q0-S9 and residues past N63 (entry 1-10, 65-69) have strongly reduced R1 and NOE from terminal fraying (R19335-J1, r1); the core C10-N63 is uniform (R1 2.26 ± 0.13 s-1, NOE 0.71 ± 0.04; J2, measured_not_detected). Native CCL5 oligomers also have a very flexible N terminus, but without values (J9, r7, other construct).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window, qualitative only. M5-S9 (entry 6-10) show increased R2 read as µs-ms motion (J3) and Y14, G32 (entry 15, 33) are exchange-broadened (J4); the rest of the core has uniform R2 at one field (J5). No dispersion, kex, population or Δω exists. Other constructs: possible intermediate exchange at basic residues of the sulfate-bound 12AAA14 mutant (J15, artefact_suspected).
per_window.slower_than_ms: search_insufficient (J26). Refolding, H/D exchange and multitemperature data are absent from the rows.
per_window.undetermined: Self-association: the entry construct stays monomeric with one resonance set (J6); native-N-terminus E66S CCL5 shows separate monomer and dimer peak sets (J10 at 310/293 K, J11 at 1/20 µM), and K25S, 12AAA14 and the engineered tetramer change assembly (J12, J13, J14, J16). Detergent FC-12 darkens the core (J7, artefact_suspected). Binding kinetics with Nt-CCR5, Nt-ECL3, Ev4 peptide and Evasin-4 (J18-J22). Static or bound structures: 1EQT helix length (J8), 6LOG register shift (J17), receptor-bound cryo-EM (J23, J24) and MD (J25). Not judged: r6 (RDC/SAXS tetramer architecture, alignment not motion), r19 and r28 (bound-pose models), r23 and r24 (CCL3 homolog MD), r32 (two unresolved C-terminal residues in 5UIW), r33 (Monte Carlo model), r38 and r39 (P2-RANTES crystal tetramer and 90% monomer/10% dimer at 1 M NaCl, oligomer populations), and abstract-only static structures r12, r29, r30, r31, r40.

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, qualitatively and without rate or population: free monomeric 5P12-RANTES-E66S (the entry sequence) at 37 °C, pH 3.8 in phosphate shows µs-ms signs only as raised 15N R2 at M5-S9 (entry 6-10) inside the frayed N-terminal tail and exchange broadening at Y14 and G32 (entry 15, 33); no dispersion was recorded, so there is no kex, population or Δω.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 19335 holds 600 MHz T1, T2 and NOE for 63 residues (no prolines) in entry numbering, with sample metadata pH 3.8 and 273 K. The deposited core (entry 11-64 without 15 and 33) averages R1 2.26 ± 0.13 s-1, R2 6.07 ± 0.78 s-1 and NOE 0.71 ± 0.04, the paper's 37 °C core values. NOE below 0.65 flags entry 1-2, 5-11, 17-18, 33-34, 39 and 67-69; R2/R1 above 3.976 flags only Y15 (author Y14; R2 16.0 s-1). G33 (author G32) has R2 13.1 s-1 but NOE 0.6485, so the screen calls it fast. M6-S10 (author M5-S9) carry R2 5.5-10.0 s-1 with NOE below 0.45.
open_conflicts: Temperature of the deposited set: the paper's Figure 4 and Methods give 37 °C, BMRB 19335 metadata gives 273 K; the deposited core averages equal the paper's 37 °C values (r1, deposition readback).
Detergent buffer for the FC-12 samples: Figure 6 says 50 mM KH2PO4, Methods say 50 mM DCOONa, and FC-12 is 1% in Figure 6 but 0.5% in the text (r3, r4).
questions_for_gina: Is the RelaxDB 19335 set the 2013 37 °C 5P12-RANTES-E66S data, so the 273 K in the BMRB metadata is a deposition error?
Should native-N-terminus CCL5 data (E66S, P9S, 12AAA14, K25S) count toward this 5P12 entry only as inference, as done here, given that their N termini and oligomer states differ?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The RelaxDB entry is the engineered variant 5P12-RANTES-E66S, so is_wt_apo true here means the unmodified entry construct, free and monomeric; native-sequence CCL5 and its mutants are other constructs and use inference_from_mutant. The entry data are in 50 mM phosphate at pH 3.8 with no phosphate-free control; CCL5 has a basic anion/GAG-binding surface, but no phosphate effect is shown. Q0 cyclises to pyroglutamate during storage, which changes Q0/G1 shifts chemically. Monomer-dimer and higher-oligomer equilibria are kept out of every window answer as self-association. Second read: r1 (residue list, corrected), r24, r34 (method, corrected) and r35 (confirmed) were flagged; the CSV carries the corrections.
